      "text": "Sounding objects can vibrate freely.\nAn external periodic force can drive them.\nIf the force's frequency is near their natural frequency, resonance can greatly boost the response.",

      "text": "Two identical tuning forks demonstrate **sound resonance**.\nSet them a short distance apart on wooden resonance boxes.\nLet the box openings face each other (Figure 83).\n\nTap one arm of one fork with a small hammer.\nThe other fork soon begins to sound as well.\nSound waves from the first apply a periodic force to it.\n\nTheir matching natural frequencies allow a large response.\nThe response depends on the frequency difference.\nOutside the receiving fork's narrow resonance band, it is much weaker.\n\nAttach a light metal clip to either identical fork.\nThis shifts its natural frequency and can detune the pair.\nWith enough detuning, the response may become inaudible.",
      "id": null,
      "label": null,
      "printed_page": 112,
      "source_refs": [
        "p0122#5",
        "p0122#8"
      ],
      "source_text": "用两个相同的音叉，观察**声的共鸣**，是最简单不过的了。把两个音叉放置在相隔不远的距离处，并使它们的木箱开口彼此相对（图83）。用小锤敲一下一个音叉的一个臂，我们很快就可以发现，第二个音叉也开始鸣响了。第一个音叉发出来的声波造成了作用于第二个音叉的周期性的力。两个音叉的固有频率相同，第二个音叉的振幅也是够大。如果取具有不同的固有频率的两个音叉，那么实际上第二个音叉在第一个音叉的激发下不会鸣响。只要在两个相同的音叉中的一个音叉上固定一个轻的金属卡子，共鸣就没有了。",
